parole.testo: From Old Church Slavonic врьтоградъ (vrĭtogradŭ), from Proto-Germanic *urtigardaz (“garden”), from *urtiz (“plant; field; garden”) + *gardaz (“enclosure; court, yard; garden”). Cognate with English orchard, Gothic 𐌰𐌿𐍂𐍄𐌹𐌲𐌰𐍂𐌳𐍃 (aurtigards, “garden”), Swedish örtagård (“herb garden”).
Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic хѫдожьство (xǫdožĭstvo). Ultimately from Proto-Germanic *handuz.
